result:
The write succeeded with no blocking lint errors this time (round 2), unlike round 1 which had 24. The manifest at `/out/manifest.json` now passes the mechanical checks: all 20 source files under `src/requests/` are partitioned across 13 Logical Units (or explicitly excluded), all cross-unit dependencies target named entrypoints, and every unit declares its effects.

Summary of the decomposition (the `requests` HTTP library):

**Domain units** (what the library is about): `public-api`, `session`, `http-message-model`, `auth`, `exceptions`, `status-codes`

**Infra units** (how it talks to the world/itself): `transport-adapter`, `cookie-jar`, `hooks`, `http-utils`, `compat-primitives`, `diagnostics`, `version-metadata`

All 166 tracked repo files are accounted for — 19 `.py` files partitioned into the 13 units, and everything else (tests, docs, CI config, brand assets, packaging files) explicitly excluded with reasons. Three real architectural seams are flagged in `violations_observed`: the hooks registration/dispatch split across two units, an implicit runtime coupling between `auth` and `transport-adapter` via a dynamically-attached attribute, and `http-utils` being an internally mixed grab-bag file. The manifest is the deliverable at `/out/manifest.json`.
